requirements.quote:
The Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data (AEAD) function
   (see [AEAD]) used for QUIC packet protection is the AEAD that is
   negotiated for use with the TLS connection.
requirements.condition: When selecting the AEAD function for QUIC packet protection.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the AEAD negotiated for the TLS connection.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using a packet-protection AEAD different from the TLS-negotiated AEAD.
requirements.why_checkable: The packet-protection algorithm can be compared with the TLS cipher-suite negotiation result.

requirements.quote:
QUIC can use any of the cipher suites defined in [TLS13] with the
   exception of TLS_AES_128_CCM_8_SHA256.
requirements.condition: When selecting a TLS cipher suite for use with QUIC.
requirements.required_behavior: Select a TLS 1.3 cipher suite other than TLS_AES_128_CCM_8_SHA256.
requirements.why_checkable: Handshake negotiation tests can inspect the cipher suite selected for a QUIC connection.

requirements.quote:
A cipher suite MUST NOT be
   negotiated unless a header protection scheme is defined for the
   cipher suite.
requirements.condition: When negotiating a cipher suite for a QUIC connection.
requirements.required_behavior: Confirm that a header-protection scheme is defined for the cipher suite before selecting it.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Negotiating a cipher suite for which no header-protection scheme is defined.
requirements.why_checkable: The negotiated suite can be checked against the implementation's defined header-protection schemes.

requirements.quote:
These cipher suites have a 16-byte
   authentication tag and produce an output 16 bytes larger than their
   input.
requirements.condition: When using a TLS 1.3 cipher suite for which this document defines QUIC header protection.
requirements.why_checkable: The AEAD output format can be measured for its authentication-tag length.

requirements.quote:
These cipher suites have a 16-byte
   authentication tag and produce an output 16 bytes larger than their
   input.
requirements.condition: When applying the selected AEAD to packet plaintext.
requirements.required_behavior: Produce ciphertext output exactly 16 bytes larger than the plaintext input.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Producing an AEAD output with a different length expansion.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can compare plaintext and AEAD-output lengths.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint MUST NOT reject a ClientHello that offers a cipher suite
   that it does not support, or it would be impossible to deploy a new
   cipher suite.  This also applies to TLS_AES_128_CCM_8_SHA256.
requirements.condition: When a ClientHello includes an unsupported cipher suite, including TLS_AES_128_CCM_8_SHA256.
requirements.required_behavior: Continue processing the ClientHello without rejecting it merely for offering that suite.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Rejecting the ClientHello solely because it offers an unsupported cipher suite.
requirements.why_checkable: A ClientHello containing an extra unsupported suite can be supplied while observing whether processing continues.

requirements.quote:
When constructing packets, the AEAD function is applied prior to
   applying header protection; see Section 5.4.
requirements.condition: When constructing a protected QUIC packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Apply the AEAD function before applying header protection.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Applying header protection before the AEAD function.
requirements.why_checkable: Cryptographic call ordering can be observed during packet construction.

requirements.quote:
When processing packets,
   an endpoint first removes the header protection.
requirements.condition: When processing a protected QUIC packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Remove header protection before subsequent packet processing and AEAD deprotection.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Attempting AEAD deprotection before removing header protection.
requirements.why_checkable: Receive-path instrumentation can verify the order of header unprotection and AEAD processing.

requirements.quote:
The key and IV for the packet are computed as described in
   Section 5.1.
requirements.condition: When computing the key and IV for QUIC packet protection.
requirements.required_behavior: Compute both according to the packet-protection key derivation defined in Section 5.1.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using a key or IV produced by a different derivation.
requirements.why_checkable: Derived key and IV bytes can be compared against key-derivation test vectors.

requirements.quote:
The 62 bits of the
   reconstructed QUIC packet number in network byte order are left-
   padded with zeros to the size of the IV.
requirements.condition: When encoding the reconstructed packet number for AEAD nonce formation.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent the 62-bit reconstructed QUIC packet number in network byte order.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using host byte order or a packet-number representation other than the reconstructed 62-bit value.
requirements.why_checkable: Nonce-construction inputs can be compared byte-for-byte with a network-order packet-number encoding.

requirements.quote:
The 62 bits of the
   reconstructed QUIC packet number in network byte order are left-
   padded with zeros to the size of the IV.
requirements.condition: After encoding the reconstructed packet number for nonce formation.
requirements.required_behavior: Left-pad the packet-number encoding with zero bytes to the size of the IV.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Right-padding it or using nonzero padding.
requirements.why_checkable: The padded packet-number buffer can be inspected for length, alignment, and zero padding.

requirements.quote:
The exclusive OR of the
   padded packet number and the IV forms the AEAD nonce.
requirements.condition: After padding the reconstructed packet number to the IV size.
requirements.required_behavior: Form the AEAD nonce by bitwise exclusive OR of the padded packet number and the IV.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using concatenation, addition, or another combining operation.
requirements.why_checkable: The produced nonce can be compared byte-for-byte with the XOR result.

requirements.quote:
The associated data, A, for the AEAD is the contents of the QUIC
   header, starting from the first byte of either the short or long
   header, up to and including the unprotected packet number.
requirements.condition: When constructing AEAD associated data for a short-header or long-header packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the contiguous QUIC-header bytes from the first header byte through and including the unprotected packet number.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Excluding a byte in that range or including payload bytes after the packet number.
requirements.why_checkable: The associated-data buffer can be compared directly with the specified header byte range.

requirements.quote:
The input plaintext, P, for the AEAD is the payload of the QUIC
   packet, as described in [QUIC-TRANSPORT].
requirements.condition: When selecting plaintext input for packet AEAD protection.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the QUIC packet payload as plaintext P.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Including the QUIC header in plaintext P or omitting packet-payload bytes.
requirements.why_checkable: The AEAD plaintext input can be compared with the serialized packet payload.

requirements.quote: The output ciphertext, C, of the AEAD is transmitted in place of P.
requirements.condition: After applying the AEAD to plaintext P.
requirements.required_behavior: Transmit ciphertext C in the packet position otherwise occupied by P.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Transmitting plaintext P or placing C outside the payload position.
requirements.why_checkable: Serialized wire bytes can be compared with the AEAD ciphertext output and plaintext payload location.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint MUST initiate a key update
   (Section 6) prior to exceeding any limit set for the AEAD that is in
   use.
requirements.condition: Before packet use under a key and IV would exceed any limit of the active AEAD.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Continuing to use the key and IV past an AEAD usage limit.
requirements.why_checkable: Usage counters can be driven to a configured AEAD limit and compared with the key-update event.
